clue.text: Many suggestions heard for production of fabric

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase is to be spoken and the spelling taken from how it sounds

parts.note: Many is C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, and suggestions are HINTS, together C HINTS

explanation.surface: Lots of ideas are being floated about how to make some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: C (a hundred, so 'many') plus HINTS, said together, sounds like the fabric; 'for production of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed printed cotton cloth, often flowery, used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Voices he trained to be in unison

indicators.note: trained suggests a choir's voices being drilled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A choirmaster has trained the singers to sing together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges VOICES HE; 'to be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesive means unified, holding together as one.

clue.text: Italian journalist without a lead is cold-shouldered

indicators.note: without a lead means losing its opening letter

parts.note: Signor is the Italian title for a man, so an Italian
ED, short for editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist from Italy with no story to lead on is snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cold-shouldered is to be snubbed, deliberately disregarded.

clue.text: Endless speculation about judge leading to end of case in consequence

indicators.note: about puts the shortened word for speculation around the official
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a theory is a speculation
a ref, referee, judges a game

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter

explanation.surface: Constant guesswork surrounds the judge until the case closes, with consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: THEOR (theory minus its end) goes around REF, and E is the end of 'case'.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore means as a result, for that reason.

clue.text: Secret coteries scattered around

indicators.note: letters scattered around are thrown about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Exclusive little groups are dispersed far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered around' rearranges the letters of COTERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by an inner circle, so it is effectively hidden or private.

clue.text: Squeeze on directors of advertising media

parts.note: to sandwich is to squeeze between two things
a board is a company's body of directors

explanation.surface: Pressure is put on the bosses of the advertising firms.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandwich boards are pairs of placards worn front and back by a person to advertise.

clue.text: A couple of beginners in an Alpine region

parts.note: a tyro is a novice, a beginner
L is a learner driver, the other beginner

explanation.surface: Two novice skiers in a mountain area.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is a mountainous area of western Austria and northern Italy in the Alps.

clue.text: Hitch over eastern painting inhibiting traveller's return

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a rub is a snag or hitch, as in 'there's the rub'
an icon is a religious painting of the Eastern Church

explanation.surface: A problem arises over an oriental artwork that stops a traveller coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar crossing the Rubicon was a step he could not reverse, so the name means a point of no return.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the Rubicon means passing a point of no return, the river Caesar crossed to start civil war.

clue.text: Article embraced by clever monarch

indicators.note: embraced by puts the article inside the word for clever

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is welcomed by a shrewd king.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute was an eleventh-century king of England, Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: Straight is worthless if ace is in play

indicators.note: in play means the letters are juggled about like cards in a game

explanation.surface: A poker straight is useless if the ace is part of the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges WORTHLESS IF ACE; both uses of 'is' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means by the most direct route, in a direct line.

clue.text: Husband gets mad over unwelcome dependants

parts.note: angers, used intransitively, means becomes angry
on, as in 'a talk on the subject', means about or over

explanation.surface: A husband loses his temper about the freeloaders sponging off the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on are parasitic followers who attach themselves to someone for gain.

clue.text: Flier whose departure was hastened by a little quarrel

definitions.text: Flier whose departure was hastened by a little quarrel

parts.words: Flier whose departure was hastened by a little quarrel
parts.note: a quarrel is also a crossbow bolt, a short arrow; the nursery-rhyme bird was killed by the sparrow's bow and arrow

explanation.surface: A bird flew off sooner because of a minor row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' reads as an argument but is an archer's bolt; in the rhyme 'Who killed Cock Robin?' the sparrow shoots the bird with an arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a small songbird, and Cock Robin's death by arrow is the subject of a well-known English nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Perhaps a war cry of Indian in school

indicators.note: in places the tribe's name inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A battle cry belonging to a Native American pupil at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh piercing shout, and a war cry is one example of such a yell.

clue.text: Many about to be caught in collapse of such a strike?

indicators.note: to be caught in means these pieces sit inside the word for collapse

parts.note: to wilt is to droop or collapse
D is the Roman numeral 500, a crossword 'many'
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Lots of workers are about to be trapped when an unofficial stoppage falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildcat strike is an unofficial walkout called without union backing.

clue.text: Look to all-round entertainment for the viewer

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references to mean look at
O is a ring shape, going all the way round

explanation.surface: Someone is told to check out comprehensive entertainment for audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recorded film or programme watched on a screen.

clue.text: Born orator is leading guide

indicators.note: is leading puts the orator's name in front of the abbreviation for born

parts.note: Cicero was the great Roman orator
NE, short for née, means born

explanation.surface: A natural public speaker is out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicerone is a tour guide who shows sightseers around antiquities, named after the eloquent Roman.

clue.text: Resort at back of mountains

parts.note: rear means the back
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A holiday spot lies behind the mountain chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place; read it as re-sort, sort again.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort again is to put things in a different order.

clue.text: Always accepted in payment, with deference

indicators.note: accepted in puts the word for always inside the payment

parts.note: rent is a regular payment
ever means always

explanation.surface: Always taken as rent, respectfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect.

clue.text: I'm to be ordered to doctor with dangerous ticker

indicators.note: to be ordered means these letters are to be put into a new order

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone is to be sent to a doctor with a risky heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be ordered' rearranges I'M TO BE into TIMEBO; a 'ticker' is slang for a heart, but here a clock in a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A time bomb has a clock that ticks down to its explosion, so it is a hazardous ticking device.

clue.text: Look closely at investment of money in cricket, perhaps

indicators.note: investment of means putting the money inside the creature

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect
P, penny, is money

explanation.surface: Examine the putting of money into the sport of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' suggests the British bat-and-ball game, but here it is the chirping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine carefully.

clue.text: Member in drink — and there's lots of it

indicators.note: in places the parliamentarian inside the beer

parts.note: ale is a drink
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician has had a drink, and there is plenty more available.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, more than enough of something.

clue.text: Furnish colourful environment for staff

indicators.note: environment for means the colour surrounds the staff

parts.note: puce is a purple-brown colour
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Provide bright surroundings for the workers.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce is to bring forward or supply, as in producing evidence.

clue.text: Society elite offering great amusement

parts.note: the cream is the best, the elite

explanation.surface: The upper-class set offer a lot of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is informally a very funny person or thing.

clue.text: Prepare to sail — from The Needles?

explanation.surface: Getting ready to leave port from the chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are chalk rocks off the Isle of Wight, but here they are knitting needles, from which stitches are finished off.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a boat's moorings and depart is one sense; to finish knitting by taking stitches off the needles is the other.

clue.text: Animal spotters to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the word is used

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers spot a creature, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a fish-eating river mammal.

clue.text: A saintly band?

parts.note: band suggests a group of holy people but means a ring of light around a holy head

explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a company of saints, but it is a circular ring of light shown in paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: An aureole is a halo or radiance encircling the head of a holy figure in religious art.

clue.text: Put up before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Something was raised ahead of a hearing in the law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect is to build or raise something upright.

clue.text: Make an impression when brought in to strengthen an agreement

indicators.note: brought in to tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to inure is to harden or toughen
to dent is to make an impression in a surface

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make their mark when called in to bolster a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal contract, especially binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Mr Toad, say, finding peak in damp surroundings

indicators.note: damp surroundings means the word for damp forms a shell around the peak

parts.note: moist means damp
a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: The Wind in the Willows hero discovers a hilltop in wet weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad in The Wind in the Willows is obsessed with motor cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad is a famously reckless car driver in Kenneth Grahame's children's novel, an example of a road user.

clue.text: Ambassador admitted to first-class order

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside the word for first-class

parts.note: best means first-class
HE, His Excellency, is the form of address for an ambassador

explanation.surface: A diplomat is given entry to a first-class carriage on command.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or instruction, as in 'at the king's behest'.
